elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New 18.8: "Teleglobe USA Inc. (the \"Customer\") may terminate this Agreement as to the Customer, and its participation in this Agreement, for convenience at any time, whether during or after the Initial Period" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right. (There are no Order Forms in this consortium construct, so agreement-level exit is the operative equivalent.)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 18.8 requires "not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties" — exactly the 30-day ceiling, in writing.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.8: "the other Parties shall refund to the Customer, pro rata, any charges prepaid by the Customer in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination." "Pro rata" is express, not inferred, and the refund runs from the counterparties to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met and unamended: 18.1 permits a Party to terminate its participation only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter" on one (1) year's notice — the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the committed 25-year Initial Period, so it is natural-term exit, not mid-term convenience; 18.2 makes any in-term termination possible only "by agreement in writing of all the Parties," i.e. with Customer's consent. New 18.8 confers the additional right on Customer only and gives the other Parties nothing.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 18.8 fixes notice at thirty (30) days, which is outside the 60–90 day band (and more favourable to us). Fallback band is therefore literally unmet; irrelevant because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: 18.8 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty or contingent payment on Customer, and the retained 18.4 no-capital-credit rule is expressed only for terminations "in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1," so no fee mechanic attaches to the new right.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 18.1 (retained) permits unilateral Party termination only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; in-term termination requires unanimous written agreement under 18.2.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing," exceeding the 90-day floor.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted Subparagraph 18.8 supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and the express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, while retained 18.1/18.2 already deny the counterparties any mid-term convenience exit (18.1's effective date is anchored to the end of the Initial Period, and 18.2 requires unanimity).

Minimal: nothing is deleted or paraphrased; 18.1, 18.2, the 18.4 no-capital-credit rule and the 18.7 liability apportionment are left verbatim. The insertion carries no survival tail, no extra damages categories, no procedure or boilerplate — only the words needed for the three unmet preferred elements, plus the anchoring phrases "In addition to Subparagraph 18.1" and "whether during or after the Initial Period," which are needed to make the right operative against the 25-year lock-in rather than extras.

Preserves intent: the redline is additive and Customer-only; it does not grant the other Parties a new exit, does not disturb the Management Committee retirement mechanic in 18.2, the 90% voting threshold, the 18.4 capital-cost rule or the 18.7 apportionment, and leaves no undefined term ("Customer" is defined in-line) or dangling cross-reference.

Deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a baseline/mechanical artefact — it reflects the pre-redline paragraph 18 text (which indeed contained no Customer convenience right, confirming the deviation) and is contradicted in substance by the rendered 18.8, which states the right expressly. Substantive inspection controls.

Optional polish (not a defect and not required for completeness): 18.4 and 18.7 are drafted by reference to "Subparagraph 18.1" only, so a termination under 18.8 falls outside both the no-capital-credit rule and the liability-survival apportionment. That asymmetry favours us and creates no contradiction, but expect the counterparties to ask that 18.7 be cross-referenced to 18.8; conceding that is acceptable, conceding 18.4 is not.
